events.title: Moby-Dick Is Published in the United States
events.description: Herman Melville's epic novel of Captain Ahab and his obsessive hunt for the white whale was first published in the United States. It sold poorly at first and baffled many critics.
events.significance: Now regarded as one of the greatest American novels, Moby-Dick went from commercial disappointment to a cornerstone of world literature.

events.title: Nellie Bly Begins Her Race Around the World
events.description: Pioneering journalist Nellie Bly set off from New York aboard a steamer. She aimed to beat the fictional 80-day journey in Jules Verne's novel by circling the globe faster.
events.significance: She finished in just over 72 days. The trip made her a global celebrity and showed what a determined woman reporter could do.

events.title: Coventry Blitz
events.description: German bombers launched one of the most concentrated air raids on a British city in the Second World War. The attack on the evening of November 14 devastated Coventry and its industry.
events.significance: The raid destroyed much of the city center, including its medieval cathedral. Coventry later became a symbol of resilience and of postwar reconciliation.

events.title: Birth of the Future King Charles III
events.description: Charles Philip Arthur George was born to Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh.
events.significance: After decades as heir to the throne, he became King of the United Kingdom and head of the Commonwealth.

events.title: Apollo 12 Launches
events.description: Apollo 12 lifted off from the Kennedy Space Center. It became the second crewed mission to land on the Moon.
events.significance: The mission showed that NASA could land precisely and carry out longer lunar explorations, building on Apollo 11's first landing.
